text: The most common freelancing mistake is not bad proposals or weak skills.
It is underpricing, charging 2 ,000 Kenyan shillings for work that took 4 hours and is worth 8 ,000 Kenyan shillings to the client.
Once you understand how clients think about price, you will never undercharge again.
In this lesson, clients do not hire on price.
They hire on value and risk.
A client choosing between a $400 proposal and a $700 proposal is not thinking the $400 one is cheaper.
They are thinking the $400 one is cheaper and riskier.
They might not deliver and I'll lose my time fixing it.
The $700 proposal wins when it reduces perceived risk more than the price difference increases cost.
Pricing models.
Hourly rate versus fixed price.
Hourly rate is safe for projects where scope is unclear.
You get paid for every hour you work.
Risk.
Clients hate open -ended hourly costs and may micromanage your hours.
Fixed price is preferable for clients and for your cash flow.
They know the total cost.
You know your income.
Disputes are rare.
Risk.
If you underestimate the hours, you eat the difference.
Recommendation.
Use fixed price for projects where you can scope clearly, chatbot builds, data analysis projects, automation workflows.
Use hourly for open -ended consulting or ongoing support contracts.
Pricing a fixed price project.
One.
Estimate hours accurately.
The most common mistake is multiplying your best case estimate by 1 .5 when you should multiply by 2.
Add 20 % for client revision rounds.
All clients request changes.
Multiply hours by your target hourly rate.
Add a 10 % risk buffer for anything you are doing for the first time.
If your number feels too high to say out loud, say it anyway.
The client's reaction to your price tells you whether you have found the right client at the right rate.
Contracts.
Always work through Upwork's payment system.
Never accept bank transfers or emperse payments for Upwork clients.
The Upwork escrow protects you.
For projects over $500, request that the client funds milestone escrow before you start work.
Milestones should be 50 % at project start, 50 % at delivery.
Never deliver the final work before the completion payment is released.
Receiving payment in Kenya.
Upwork pays to pay a near or direct bank transfer.
Pay a near is recommended.
It gives you a US virtual bank account that makes receiving dollars from any platform faster and cheaper.
Set up takes 2 -3 business days from Kenya.
Apply what you learn in this lesson and you will see results immediately.
Your skills bear fruit.
